meta.title: AMDL: Apple Music to your own disk, lossless and tagged
meta.description: AMDL is a self-hosted, open-source downloader. Paste an Apple Music link or search the catalog, and it saves finished, tagged .m4a files: ALAC up to 24-bit/192 kHz, Dolby Atmos or AAC. Use it from a web console, the desktop app, a terminal, or an AI agent over MCP.
meta.ogAlt: AMDL: Apple Music, on your own disk.

hero.title:
Apple Music,
on your own disk.
hero.lead: Paste a song, album, playlist, artist or station link, or search the catalog. AMDL downloads, decrypts, remuxes and tags every track into a finished `.m4a`, and keeps a record of what is on your disk. Use it from a desktop app, a web console, a terminal, or an AI agent.
hero.fine: AGPL-3.0 · macOS, Windows, Linux and Docker
hero.strip: One track's waveform in four parts, one for each stage, ending in a tagged .m4a file

shown: Illustrations of the real screens, with made-up music. Like the apps themselves, they are in English.

desktop.title: A native app, with a server or without one.
desktop.lead: Built with MyGo for macOS, Windows and Linux. On its first launch it asks where downloads run: on a server on your network, or on this computer, where it runs the backend itself and sets up ffmpeg, QEMU and the wrapper for you.
facts: macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux (amd64; Linux needs GTK 3)
A client of your AMDL server, or standalone with the backend inside the app, sharing one history with `amdl` on the same machine

Search, album pages, the queue, the library, your Apple Music library, accounts and hooks. Drop a link on the window to download it.; Settings › Connection updates, stops or removes the wrapper it runs
Ships with 2.0. The packages are not signed yet, so macOS and Windows each block the first launch once.

labels.queue: The desktop app's Queue: the running album at the top, then the queue with its filters
labels.library: The desktop app's Library: album records as a grid of covers, each marked downloaded or downloading
labels.album: The desktop app's album page: an album mid-download, track by track, with the folder it is saved to

console.title: The server's own page, in any browser.
console.lead: `amdl serve` puts the console on the same port as the API. Run it on a NAS or a Docker host and open it from any phone or laptop on the network, with nothing to install there; on your own computer it stays on loopback.
facts: `amdl serve` (port 18080 on this machine only, unless `server.listen` says otherwise), `amdl service install` (`amdl service status` prints its address) or the Docker image (port 18080)
New download, Overview, Activity (the queue, reordered by dragging), Settings and Logs, plus your Apple Music library once you switch it on
Sign in to Apple Music with two-step verification, change the config with a save bar and restart (a few keys stay file-only), and edit hooks
Light and dark, a command palette and keyboard shortcuts; a sidebar, an icon rail or bottom tabs, down to a phone

labels.new: The console's New download page: search results for a made-up artist, albums with their quality and songs with a download button
labels.overview: The console's Overview: a link that failed, under Needs attention, then the live queue as cards in each album's colors
labels.logs: The console's Logs page: the backend's log records with their level and component

terminal.title: For people at a prompt, and for scripts.
terminal.lead: The same `amdl` binary is the client for both, talking to your server, the one this machine runs, or a backend it starts itself with `--server embedded`.

tui.title: Terminal UI
tui.text: `amdl` with no arguments opens an interactive interface that prints into your scrollback. Paste a link, or type to search; up to three jobs follow as cards, with an album bar and each track's stage.
facts: `/quality` orders the codecs, `/queue` reorders the queue, and `/library`, `/jobs`, `/retry`, `/logs` and `/login` do what they say
Enter downloads, Space selects, Tab filters, shift+↑↓ moves a job; `/help` lists them all
Follows a light or dark terminal; with `NO_COLOR` the bars still read by their shapes
tui.label: The terminal UI: the banner, a running album as a card with each track's stage, the prompt and search results for a made-up artist

cli.title: Command line
cli.text: Every command prints one JSON value on stdout, and an error as JSON on stderr with its own exit status, so it pipes into `jq` and scripts. Streams are NDJSON.
facts: `search`, `download`, `jobs`, `library`, `apple-library`, `accounts`, `hooks`, `config`, `wrapper`, `logs`, `system` and more. `--server`, `AMDL_URL` or a context saved with `amdl context add` picks the server
`--dry-run` on every change, a confirmation before anything destructive, and `--fields` to keep only what you need
`amdl cli search "<what you want>"` and `amdl schema <command>`
`amdl doctor` checks the server, ffmpeg, the wrapper and the service, and prints the command that installs what is missing
cli.label: A terminal session: a catalog search piped into jq, a download streaming its tracks through download, decrypt, remux and tag, and a job list

agents.title: Hand it to an agent, or wire it into your setup.
agents.lead: An MCP server for AI agents, an HTTP API for your own tools, and hooks that tell the rest of your setup when a download is done.

mcp.title: MCP server
mcp.text: `amdl mcp` serves the command line's capabilities as 37 MCP tools over stdio. `amdl cli setup` prints the config for Claude Code, Codex or any `mcpServers` client, and an agent skill. No tool signs in, so an Apple ID password never passes through a model.
mcp.ask: Download the new Mira Solenne album in Dolby Atmos.
mcp.reply: Done: Glass Weather (2025), all 12 tracks in Dolby Atmos, saved to `/volume1/music/library/Mira Solenne/Glass Weather/`.
mcp.label: An agent conversation: the agent calls search_catalog, start_download and wait_for_job, then says where the album was saved
mcp.config: The client config `amdl cli setup` prints

api.title: HTTP API
api.text: REST and Server-Sent Events under `/api/v1`, on the console's port. The OpenAPI 3.1 spec is in the repository, every error has the same shape, and a stream picks up where it left off. Responses carry no CORS headers: the console is the API's only browser client.

hooks.title: Hooks
hooks.text: Call a webhook or run a command when a job is queued, finishes, fails or is cancelled. Presets fill in ntfy, Bark or Telegram notifications and Plex, Jellyfin or Emby library refreshes, and a notification waits until a failure will not be retried. Test sends one with a sample payload, a body is a Go template over the payload, and command hooks are edited only in the file.
hooks.label: The console's Settings › Hooks: the switch that runs hooks, and the presets to add one from

specs.title: What happens behind every link.
specs.lead: One server keeps the queue, the records of what you own and the folder they live in.

formats.text: List the codecs you want, in order: ALAC, Dolby Atmos, Dolby Digital and three kinds of AAC. Each gets its own retries; when one runs out, the next takes over, with AAC-LC as the last resort. ALAC goes up to 24-bit/192 kHz, or a ceiling you set.

records.text: Each album and playlist is kept per track and per quality. A failed track is retried by later runs, after 30 minutes and then 2 hours, until it gives up. Pause, resume, download again (only the lyrics or the covers, if that is all you want), add a second quality as its own file, delete a record and keep its files, or check the disk for files that went missing: a check that finds more than half missing stops, so an unmounted share is not written off.
records.label: Twelve tracks of a record: ten downloaded, one waiting to retry, one missing

library.text: Songs, albums and artists share one folder tree, laid out by a template; playlists and stations get folders of their own. A file already in place is adopted, not downloaded again, unless `download.overwrite_existing` is on.

accounts.text: A wrapper-manager holds up to ten Apple Music accounts. A link is read in its own region's catalog when one of them serves it, and an album missing from one region is tried in the others. One is the default, the order decides which one serves a region, and `amdl accounts delete` removes one.

wrapper.text: amdl holds no Apple account: your login stays in the wrapper. Use wrapper-manager v2 (up to ten accounts) or a single wrapper-lite, or let `amdl wrapper install` run one: natively on Linux x86_64 with user namespaces, in a QEMU guest elsewhere (software-emulated on Apple Silicon; not on Windows on ARM), with `update`, `start`, `stop`, `logs` and `uninstall` beside it. A wrapper behind a gateway takes a `wrapper.token` (`amdl wrapper keygen` makes one), and there is a Cloudflare template; mainland China blocks `workers.dev`, so bind your own domain.

lyrics.text: Tags, a cover up to 5000×5000 and lyrics go into the file: LRC timed by line or by word, with translation and romanization if you want them, and `.lrc` or `.ttml` files beside it. Album, artist and playlist covers are saved next to the music.

sync.text: Add a song to your Apple Music library on your phone, and its whole album downloads at home: amdl checks each account you switch on every 15 minutes. It is off by default, and switching it on starts from your library as it is, without downloading the past. You can browse a copy of your Apple Music library too, and download a playlist with no catalog link song by song.

groups.title: Links
items: Songs, albums, playlists (shared `pl.u-` ones too), artists and radio stations, from music.apple.com and classical.music.apple.com
Up to 100 links at once; `amdl download -` reads them from stdin
A preview and a quality check before anything downloads
A station is a rolling list: the tracks Apple offers now, not a fixed one
An album link with `?i=` downloads that one song (`catalog.album_track_url_mode` can make it the album); an artist link adds every album, or only the albums without singles
Search another region's catalog with `--storefront`, and open an artist's albums a page at a time (→ in the TUI)
Not supported: music videos, and live radio such as Apple Music 1

groups.title: Queue
items: Reorder by dragging, with shift+↑↓ in the TUI, or `amdl jobs move`; Download now jumps the line
Three jobs at a time and sixteen parallel transfers by default, both adjustable
Jobs survive a restart, and an interrupted transfer resumes
An add that fails stays pending until you retry or delete it

groups.title: Your files
items: Files land in `~/Music/AMDL` (`%UserProfile%\Music\AMDL` on Windows) with the binary, in `./data/downloads` with Docker
No decrypted whole track is written to disk: the samples go straight into ffmpeg
An integrity check after each track
Downloading again replaces a file only once the new one is complete
Apple's rate limits are respected, with a cooldown when Apple asks for one
Changing the language or the template, or Apple renaming an album, makes the files at the old paths count as missing

groups.title: Running it
items: `amdl service install` starts the backend at login: a LaunchAgent, a systemd user unit or a Task Scheduler task
Simulate mode runs the whole pipeline without a wrapper or ffmpeg, to try it out
Settings apply at once; the few that need a restart get it from the console
Recent logs, live in the console or `amdl logs tail`
Download statistics on the Overview, or `amdl system stats`
Upgrade by running the install script again, which puts the old binary back if the new one fails; `amdl service uninstall` and `amdl wrapper uninstall --purge` remove it

groups.title: Docker and NAS
items: One image for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, with ffmpeg inside, a health check and `PUID`/`PGID`
Notes for Synology shares, `/dev/kvm` and reverse proxies

groups.title: Speed
items: Decryption runs inside amdl: a 12-track ALAC album now takes about 39–41 s instead of 51–55 s
AMDL-Web's wrapper fork served 3,450 keys in a row without a failure, with the median key time down from about 1.17 s to 0.59 s

groups.title: From 1.x
items: The database migrates on the first start; back it up first, since 1.x cannot read it afterwards
The image, the wrapper and the path settings changed: [the upgrade guide]({blob}/docs/upgrading-to-2.0.md) has the checklist
Files 1.x saved under `songs/`, `albums/` and `artists/` are not moved or recognised: asking for them again downloads them again
Queued or running 1.x jobs come back as paused adds, and environment variables no longer set config keys

groups.title: Languages
items: The apps are in English; names, genres and lyric translations follow `catalog.language`
`catalog.language` is Simplified Chinese (`zh-Hans_CN`) out of the box: set it before the first download, since changing it later renames what new downloads write
This site and the README are in English and Simplified Chinese

groups.title: Good to know
items: Stations, library sync, your Apple Music library and private playlist covers need a wrapper that hands out each account's media-user-token, as AMDL-Web's fork does
wrapper-lite does not verify Apple's TLS certificates
The console plays Apple's animated album covers; `catalog.motion_artwork_enabled` turns the lookup off

install.title: Up and running in a few minutes.
install.lead: You need an Apple Music subscription and a wrapper: the service that holds your Apple Music login. Run the wrapper on a Linux box, or let amdl run it on your own machine: natively on Linux x86_64, in a QEMU guest on other systems except Windows on ARM.

steps.title: Install amdl
steps.text: The script checks the release against its `SHA256SUMS` and puts `amdl` in `~/.local/bin`, printing the line to add to `PATH` if that folder is not on it. On Windows it goes to your user programs folder.

steps.title: Check ffmpeg
steps.text: Every track goes through ffmpeg, 8 or later. `amdl doctor` says whether this machine has it, and prints the command that installs it if not.

steps.title: Get a wrapper
steps.text: This downloads the wrapper guest AMDL-Web publishes and checks it against a pinned hash. On Linux x86_64 where `unshare -Ur true` succeeds it runs the wrapper natively; elsewhere it needs QEMU, which it offers to install on macOS and Windows and names the package for on Linux. Already run a wrapper on a NAS or server? Skip this step.

steps.title: Run the backend
steps.text: This registers the backend as a service that starts at login, and it starts the wrapper with it. For a wrapper elsewhere, add `--wrapper <its address>`. `amdl service status` prints the console's address: sign in on its Account page, or here with `amdl wrapper login`.

steps.title: Get the Compose file
steps.text: In an empty directory. It runs the image `ghcr.io/amdl-web/apple-music-downloader`. Create `data/downloads` first and give it to the backend's user (`PUID:PGID`, 1000:1000 unless you set them); otherwise Docker creates it as root.

steps.title: Turn on the wrapper
steps.text: In `docker-compose.yml`, uncomment the `wrapper-manager` service and the `volumes:` block at the end of the file.

steps.title: Start both
steps.text: Compose builds wrapper-manager from the `amdl` branch of AMDL-Web's wrapper fork, so the host needs internet access.

steps.title: Point at the wrapper and sign in
steps.text: Open `http://localhost:18080/`, go to **Settings › Account**, set **Session service** to the address below, save and restart from the notice. Then sign in with your Apple ID and paste a link into **New download**; finished files land in `./data/downloads`.

nas.label: NAS
nas.text: The wrapper needs user namespaces: `unshare -Ur true` must succeed. On a host without them, such as Synology DSM, use wrapper-manager v2's QEMU variant, which needs `/dev/kvm`.

install.more: Every option of both paths is in the [install guide]({blob}/docs/install.md) and the [deployment guide]({blob}/docs/deployment.md). Coming from 1.x? Read [upgrading to 2.0]({blob}/docs/upgrading-to-2.0.md) first.
install.prerelease: Until 2.0.0 is released, the script and the `latest` image still mean an older release: pass a 2.0 release candidate's tag with `--version` (`-Version` on Windows), and use that tag in place of `latest` in the Compose file. Homebrew and Scoop arrive with 2.0.1. A database written by rc.1 to rc.7 cannot be opened: move it aside to start empty.

notice: AMDL needs your own Apple Music subscription and is for personal use: each install serves one person. It relies on Apple's undocumented web-player API, which can change without notice.
